answer: When an AI agent claims a new identity, the protocol locks its reward in a vesting contract that releases tokens only after a schedule tied to proven work on the network’s terrace of tasks. Each release forces the agent to stake fresh proof‑of‑work, so a sybil farm must front‑load the full stake for every identity, driving cost to the nadir of profitability before any payout. Thus the reward becomes a fable of delayed gain, making mass registration unprofitable for an attacker.
